source: KDIGO 2023 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD Evaluation
text: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is classified by sustained reduction in glomerular filtration rate: Stage 1 (eGFR >= 90 with kidney damage/albuminuria), Stage 2 (eGFR 60-89, mild decline), Stage 3a (eGFR 45-59, mild-moderate), Stage 3b (eGFR 30-44, moderate-severe), Stage 4 (eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73m2, severely decreased), and Stage 5 (eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73m2, kidney failure/end-stage renal disease). Staging strictly directs diagnostic coding and specialist nephrology referral.

Metformin is recommended as first-line therapy in patients with Type 2 Diabetes and CKD when eGFR >= 45 mL/min/1.73m2 (Stage 1-3a). Metformin dose should be halved if eGFR is between 30 and 44 mL/min/1.73m2 (Stage 3b). Metformin is strictly contraindicated in advanced CKD with eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2 (Stage 4 and Stage 5) due to the substantial risk of fatal lactic acidosis.

topic: RAAS Blockade & Calcium Channel Blockers in Advanced CKD
text: Initiating or escalating high-dose ACE inhibitors (e.g., Lisinopril) or ARBs in advanced CKD Stage 4 or Stage 5 (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2) carries severe risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia and acute precipitously dropped glomerular filtration. Dihydropyridine Calcium Channel Blockers (such as Amlodipine) are preferred first-line alternative antihypertensive agents in severe renal impairment as they preserve renal hemodynamics without elevating serum potassium.

source: KDIGO 2023 Guideline for Kidney Disease Evaluation
topic: Differential Diagnosis: Acute Kidney Injury vs Chronic Kidney Disease
text: When eGFR is depressed, clinical history must differentiate between acute kidney injury (rapid rise in serum creatinine within hours to days) and chronic kidney disease (sustained eGFR reduction >= 3 months). In chronic presentations with longstanding cardiometabolic history, bilateral renal changes and persistent proteinuria, chronic kidney disease staging is verified.

source: ACC/AHA 2017 Guideline for High Blood Pressure in Adults
topic: Blood Pressure Staging and Diagnostic Thresholds
text: Blood pressure categories in adults: Normal Blood Pressure (Systolic BP < 120 mmHg and Diastolic BP < 80 mmHg); Elevated Blood Pressure (SBP 120-129 mmHg and DBP < 80 mmHg); Stage 1 Essential Hypertension (SBP 130-139 mmHg or DBP 80-89 mmHg); Stage 2 Essential Hypertension (SBP >= 140 mmHg or DBP >= 90 mmHg). Hypertensive Crisis is diagnosed when SBP > 180 mmHg and/or DBP > 120 mmHg.

source: ACC/AHA Guideline for the Prevention and Management of High Blood Pressure
text: For initial management of uncomplicated primary hypertension in patients with normal kidney function, first-line classes include ACE inhibitors (such as Lisinopril), Angiotensin Receptor Blockers (ARBs), or Calcium Channel Blockers (such as Amlodipine).

source: ADA Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes 2024
topic: Glycemic Management in Advanced Renal Impairment
text: In patients with Type 2 Diabetes and severe CKD Stage 4 or 5 where oral antidiabetic agents like Metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors are contraindicated or insufficient, Insulin therapy (basal or prandial regimens) is safe and effective. Dose adjustments are necessary to prevent hypoglycemia due to reduced renal clearance of insulin.

source: ADA Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes 2024
topic: First-Line Glycemic Therapy in Type 2 Diabetes
text: First-line therapy for Type 2 Diabetes with normal renal function or early-stage disease consists of Metformin along with comprehensive lifestyle modification. Metformin provides high glycemic efficacy, low risk of hypoglycemia, and weight neutrality.

Serum potassium exceeding 5.0 mEq/L mandates review of potassium-sparing medications and RAAS inhibitors. In CKD Stages 4-5, hyperkalemia risk escalates exponentially with Lisinopril, making Amlodipine the optimal non-potassium-affecting vasodilator.
